title: MakeMyTrip acquires majority stake in Quick Ride to enter shared mobility segment
summary:
Travel technology platform MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based shared mobility startup Quick Ride, marking its entry into the ride pooling segment. The acquisition will expand MakeMyTrip’s ground transportation portfolio and strengthen its presence in daily urban commutes.
Entrackr exclusively reported on October 19 that MakeMyTrip was in talks to acquire Quick Ride through its subsidiary redBus. However, the financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.









Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride is an asset-light mobility platform that connects people travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. It enables users to share rides for everyday commutes and offers services to corporate employees through partnerships with companies, IT parks and business campuses. The platform aims to make commuting more affordable while reducing the number of vehicles on roads.
According to MakeMyTrip, Quick Ride’s ride pooling business and brand have undergone an internal restructuring and are now housed under a new entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited. MakeMyTrip has acquired the brand and its ride pooling business through a majority stake in this entity. Quick Ride’s promoters will continue to lead the business, while its erstwhile EV taxi business will remain with the predecessor entity, iDisha Info Labs Private Limited.
Commenting on the development, Rajesh Magow, Co-founder and Group CEO of MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will help the company establish a presence in high-frequency daily commutes within cities, alongside intercity travel. He added that Quick Ride will be housed under MakeMyTrip’s ground transport business, which will leverage its experience in building redBus in India and overseas markets to scale the platform.
Prakash Sangam, CEO of redBus and Head of Ground Transport at MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will expand the company’s offerings across different travel needs. The platform sees an opportunity to serve the same customers across their daily office commutes and intercity journeys.
Quick Ride has raised funding from investors including Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners), Naspers (now part of Prosus) and Venture Highway. In 2019, the company raised Rs 100.78 crore ($14.4 million) in a Series B round from its existing investors.
The acquisition is part of MakeMyTrip’s strategy to expand its presence across travel segments through acquisitions and strategic investments. In recent years, the company has acquired Savaari in the car rental segment, Happay in corporate travel and expense management, and Flamingo Transworld in regional group holiday packages. It has also made a strategic minority investment in visa processing platform Atlys.
The latest acquisition adds ride pooling to its ground transportation portfolio, which already includes redBus and Savaari. The company said the addition of Quick Ride will help it offer customers a wider range of travel options, from daily commutes to intercity journeys.

title: Mamaearth parent Honasa profit jumps 87% to Rs 73 Cr in Q2 FY27, revenue grows 36%
summary:
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 36% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore.
The Gurugram-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 731 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 538 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE).

The firm also recorded Rs 22 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 753 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the expense front, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, increasing 38.4% to Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 159 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses also increased 21.7% to Rs 73 crore. Depreciation expenses, however, marginaly declined  to Rs 11 crore from Rs 11.75 crore.
Other expenses rose 26.9% to Rs 348 crore which pushed its total expenses by 29.1% to Rs 652 crore during the last quarter.
At the bottom line, Honasa Consumer’s net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39.23 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, Honasa Consumer's revenue from operations grew 31.2% to Rs 1,487 crore from Rs 1,133 crore in H1 FY26.
Meanwhile, its net profit jumped 2.03X to Rs 164 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 80.5 crore in the corresponding period last year. The firm’s total income stood at Rs 1,531 crore in H1 FY27, compared with Rs 1,177 crore in H1 FY26.
The company's shares were trading at Rs 487 as of 1:35 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 15,703 crore.

title: Angel One overtakes Zerodha to become second-largest broker; Groww adds over 3 lakh clients in October
summary:
Angel One overtook Zerodha to become India’s second-largest stock broker in October 2026, adding nearly 2.43 lakh active clients during the month. Meanwhile, Groww maintained its leadership position with over 1.37 crore active clients, while discount broking platform Sahi recorded the fastest monthly growth among the top 20 brokers.
According to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the total active client base increased 1.33% month-on-month to 4.67 crore in October from 4.61 crore in September, an addition of nearly 6.15 lakh clients.
Groww retained its dominant position with 1.37 crore active clients in October, adding the highest number of clients at 3.04 lakh during the month. Its market share stood at 29.43%, the highest among stock brokers in India.
Angel One moved to the second position with 69.98 lakh active clients, an addition of 2.43 lakh clients during the month. Its market share increased to 14.97%.
Zerodha slipped to the third position with 67.59 lakh active clients, down 32,435 from 67.91 lakh in September. Its market share stood at 14.46%.

ICICI Securities retained the fourth position with 21.64 lakh active clients, adding 3,722 clients during the month. Upstox held the fifth spot with 18.43 lakh active clients, despite a decline of 11,348 clients. Their respective market shares stood at 4.63% and 3.94%.
Among other major brokers, Kotak Securities added 12,895 clients to reach 14.05 lakh, while HDFC Securities' active client base increased to 13.60 lakh from 13.54 lakh in September.
Dhan added 25,739 active clients during October to reach 11.47 lakh, with its market share standing at 2.45%. SBI Securities saw its client base decline by 17,188 to 10.04 lakh, taking its market share to 2.15%. Motilal Oswal added 7,283 clients to reach 9.16 lakh, with a market share of 1.96%.
Paytm Money recorded the steepest decline among the top 20 brokers, with a loss of 32,501 active clients, down 4.26% month-on-month to 7.30 lakh. In contrast, INDmoney added 1,849 clients to reach 7.21 lakh.
Sahi emerged as the fastest-growing broker among the top 20 in October, following an 11% increase in its active client base in September. The platform added 34,372 clients during the month, taking its total to 3.15 lakh. Its market share stood at 0.67%.
PhonePe's Share.Market added 7,041 active clients to reach 2.14 lakh in October. IIFL Securities also added 5,095 clients, taking its active client base to 3.46 lakh.

title: Sleepy Owl’s revenue surges 86% to Rs 82 Cr in FY26; nears breakeven
summary:
Coffee has become a part of everyday conversations, with more Indians exploring different varieties and flavours. While many people prefer Brazilian or Vietnamese coffee, not everyone knows that India is the world's fifth-largest coffee exporter among coffee-producing nations, accounting for around 5% of global exports.
This growing interest has also given rise to several homegrown coffee brands trying to find their place in the market. One of them is Sleepy Owl, which has grown nearly 4X in the past three years, increasing its revenue from Rs 21.5 crore in FY23 to Rs 82 crore in FY26.


Sleepy Owl’s revenue from operations grew 86.4% year-on-year to Rs 82 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 44 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Sleepy Owl is a homegrown coffee brand focused on the at-home coffee consumption market. Its product range includes cold brew, instant coffee, hot brew bags, ground coffee, and ready-to-drink coffee.
The sale of coffees are the primary source of revenue for Sleep Owl which includes coffee seches, can, bottles, coffee packets and boxes.
On the cost side, coffee procurement accounted for around 22% of its overall expenses. This cost grew 84.3% to Rs 43.5 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also increased to Rs 9 crore during the fiscal year.
The company spent Rs 20 crore on advertising in FY26. Other expenses, including shipping, legal, technology and other operating costs, increased to Rs 85 crore from Rs 47 crore in FY25.


Sleepy Owl managed to reduce its net losses by 17% to Rs 1.76 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.12 crore in the previous fiscal year. The company is nearing breakeven, with its ROCE and EBITDA margin standing at -6% and -1.8%, respectively. On a unit level, it spent Rs 1.04 to earn every rupee of revenue in FY26.
Building a business around coffee for home consumption has not been easy, and several startups have tried to crack this market. In that sense, Sleepy Owl reaching Rs 82 crore in revenue and bringing its losses close to breakeven is a good sign for the company. The competition, however, is getting stronger. Blue Tokai and Third Wave Coffee are also growing their businesses, with the former recently raising $25 million and reportedly looking to extend its Series D round. Blue Tokai and Third Wave Coffee reported revenues of Rs 325 crore and Rs 285 crore, respectively. Established players such as Tata Starbucks and Cafe Coffee Day are much larger, with revenues of Rs 1,367 crore and Rs 1,094 crore, respectively. For Sleepy Owl, the real test will be to maintain this growth and turn the business profitable as competition in the coffee market heats up.

title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space raises $6 Mn in seed round
summary:
Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 million in a seed funding round from Japan-based Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures and existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. The latest round takes its total funding to over $9 million.
In September last year, the startup raised $3.17 million in an oversubscribed pre-seed round led by Alan Rutledge, with participation from AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.
The fresh capital will support the development of Base 1, technology demonstrations and two upcoming missions, Cosmoserve said in a press release.
The startup has also inaugurated Base 1, a private facility dedicated to space debris removal and satellite servicing. The facility is designed to support the development of technologies for in-orbit repairs, refuelling and the recovery of defunct satellites.
According to the company, Base 1 is the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation capabilities. It brings together infrastructure for designing, building, testing and operating technologies required for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.
Cosmoserve currently sources nearly 60% of its mission components locally. It aims to increase domestic manufacturing by developing critical technologies in-house and reducing dependence on imported optics, avionics and space-grade electronics.
In July 2026, Cosmoserve flew its first payload, Mission Embrace, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The flight hardware was developed in under four months, six months ahead of schedule. However, the robotic capture petals did not deploy as planned, providing the company with data for further development.
Founded last year by Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Cosmoserve is developing a proprietary Dual Spacecraft Architecture to make orbital servicing more cost-efficient. The approach uses two spacecraft to service multiple satellites, instead of the conventional one-to-one recovery model.
The company estimates that its approach could bring satellite servicing costs down from around $10 million to below $1 million per satellite.
Cosmoserve plans to test its robotic capture systems through microgravity flights, reflight Mission Embrace and conduct a full-scale space debris capture demonstration in 2027.
The startup is among a growing number of Indian spacetech companies working on technologies spanning launch vehicles, satellite manufacturing, space data and orbital infrastructure. Hyderabad has also emerged as a spacetech hub, supported by its aerospace and defence ecosystem, engineering talent and research infrastructure.

summary:

Moneyview’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,120 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 794 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 26 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,146 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 804.6 crore in Q2 FY26.
Founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview provides digital lending products such as instant personal loans, credit cards, Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and financial management solutions through partner lenders. Its lending partners include Aditya Birla Capital, Northern Arc, Vivriti Capital and Oxyzo.
Impairment of financial instruments increased 18.7% to Rs 286 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 241 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefits expenses rose 41.3% to Rs 97.5 crore from Rs 69 crore during the same period.
Finance costs increased 25.6% to Rs 194 crore from Rs 154.5 crore, while other expenses grew 24.6% to Rs 298.5 crore from Rs 239.5 crore. Overall, Moneyview's total expenses increased 24.5% to Rs 876.5 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 704 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.
At the bottom line, the company's net profit surged 5.15 times to Rs 201 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, marking a 415.4% year-on-year increase.
On a half-yearly basis, Moneyview's revenue from operations grew 45.3% to Rs 2,161 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,487 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 253.8% to Rs 375 crore from Rs 106 crore during the same period.
At the close of Thursday’s trading session, the company's shares settled at Rs 58.25, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 9,701 crore.

Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, along with a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore, taking its potential fund size to Rs 300 crore.
The first close was anchored by family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and entrepreneurs. The fund achieved the first close shortly after receiving SEBI registration in October 2026.
Led by Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Daksham Growth Ventures, the fund will primarily invest in pre-Series A and Series A companies across India’s consumer ecosystem.
DGV Fund I plans to invest Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore in businesses that have established product-market fit and sound unit economics. It will focus on companies with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25-75 crore and the potential to scale to Rs 300-500 crore in revenue.
The fund’s investment strategy spans four segments: direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C and supply chain businesses, and consumer-focused artificial intelligence (AI) companies.
Beyond capital, DGV plans to support its portfolio companies through governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion. The fund will also provide board participation, strategic guidance and access to industry networks to help businesses strengthen their organisational capabilities.
Daksham Capital operates across family office advisory, investment solutions, global investing, legacy and succession planning, investment banking advisory and structured lending solutions. The group said its team has advised more than 600 client families and previously managed over $1 billion in assets.
Daksham Growth Ventures is the group’s dedicated growth investment platform, focusing on consumer and consumer-allied businesses with established business models and the potential to scale sustainably.

Venomics AI, a biotechnology company spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), has raised $2.7 million in its first institutional funding round. The pre-seed round was co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio.
The proceeds will be used to expand the company’s operations, grow its molecular dataset and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities, Venomics AI said in a press release.
Co-founded in May 2026 by Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI combines venom biology, molecular sequencing, AI and experimental screening to discover and develop venom-derived therapeutic leads.
The Bengaluru-based startup is building the Venom Atlas, a platform that connects venom-derived molecular data with laboratory validation and drug discovery. It uses AI to prioritise molecular candidates and tests these predictions through functional screening in the laboratory. The experimental results are then fed back into subsequent predictions and molecular design.
The company aims to use India’s venom biodiversity and its scientific and computational expertise to develop a drug discovery platform for global therapeutic development.
Venomics AI has established the initial architecture of its platform, joined the NVIDIA Inception programme and been selected among the top five finalists for the 2026 Indo-Boston Biotech Bridge Award.
It plans to build a multidisciplinary team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.
Startups in this space are exploring bioactive peptides and proteins found in snake, scorpion and marine animal venoms to identify molecules with potential applications in pain management, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases and other therapeutic areas.
Another player in the space is Snaayu Lifesciences, incubated at C-CAMP, which is working on isolating and characterising novel analgesic compounds from cone snail venom.
The broader AI-driven drug discovery space has also attracted investor interest. Bengaluru-based Peptris Technologies raised Rs 70 crore in a Series A round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Speciale Invest in February 2026. The startup uses AI-driven molecular discovery and experimental validation to advance potential drug candidates.

title: Tonbo Imaging turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 23.5 Cr; shares hit 20% upper circuit
summary:
Defence technology company Tonbo Imaging reported over 20X year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in its first quarterly results (Q2 FY27) after listing on the stock exchanges. The company also turned profitable during the quarter.
Tonbo Imaging’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 183.3 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 8.9 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.

Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops advanced imaging and surveillance technologies for defence and security applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting solutions, missile seekers and fire control systems.
Tonbo Imaging's total income stood at Rs 185.2 crore during the quarter, including Rs 1.9 crore from non-operating income.
As the company scaled up its operations, its expenses also increased in line with scale. Cost of materials consumed was the largest expense component, accounting for over 78% of total expenses at Rs 120.9 crore during the quarter.
Employee benefits expenses remained largely flat at around Rs 12 crore in Q2 FY27, while depreciation and amortisation expenses and finance costs stood at Rs 9.8 crore and Rs 4.8 crore, respectively.
Overall, Tonbo Imaging's total expenses surged over 7 times year-on-year to Rs 153.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.
A 20.6X growth in operating revenue helped Tonbo Imaging turn profitable during the quarter, with a net profit of Rs 23.5 crore against a net loss of Rs 9.6 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a sequential basis, Tonbo Imaging's revenue from operations increased over 5 times from Rs 36 crore in the previous quarter. The company had reported a net loss of Rs 17.7 crore in Q2 FY26.
Following the strong quarterly performance, Tonbo Imaging's share price surged 20% and hit the upper circuit at Rs 1,530.3 apiece at 1:10 PM today, taking its market capitalisation to Rs 8,766 crore.

title: Shiprocket swings to profit in Q2 FY27; revenue rises 35% to Rs 674 Cr

The company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 674 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.


Shiprocket also earned Rs 20 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 694 crore during the quarter.
The company's core business segment continued to contribute the largest share of revenue, growing 25.3% year-on-year to Rs 461.5 crore in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, its emerging business segment, which includes cross-border shipping, omnichannel fulfilment, hyperlocal delivery and e-commerce enablement solutions such as checkout and marketing technology, surged 60.6% to Rs 212 crore from Rs 132 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the cost side, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense, rising 29.8% to Rs 479 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 369 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased 8.3% to Rs 104 crore from Rs 96 crore during the same period.
Depreciation expenses rose 47% to Rs 11.76 crore from Rs 8 crore, while other expenses increased 58.1% to Rs 98 crore from Rs 62 crore. Overall, Shiprocket's total expenses grew 29.5% to Rs 693 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 535 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, Shiprocket's operating revenue grew 34.3% to Rs 1,266 crore from Rs 943 crore in H1 FY26. Its net loss narrowed 65.8% to Rs 13.12 crore from Rs 38.32 crore during the same period.
The company's shares were trading at Rs 131.50 as of 1:07 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 9,593 crore.

title: Decathlon India’s total income crosses Rs 4,500 Cr in FY26;  EBITDA stands at Rs 424 Cr
summary:
As interest in sports beyond cricket continues to grow in India, people are increasingly taking up activities such as badminton, hockey, boxing, swimming, trekking and skating. This has also created opportunities for brands catering to a wider range of sporting needs. One such brand is Decathlon, which offers products across multiple sports categories under one roof. Let's decode how the sporting goods retailer performed financially in FY26.
French sporting goods retailer Decathlon's Indian arm reported an 8.35% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 4,478 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,133 crore in FY25.
Started in India in 2009, Decathlon has grown into one of the country's largest sporting goods retailers. The company currently operates 132 stores across India and is targeting an expansion to 200 stores by 2030.

The sale of sporting goods and apparel remains its primary source of revenue. Its product portfolio includes clothing, footwear, trekking gear, fitness equipment and accessories across various sports categories. The company also added Rs 39 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 4,517 crore in FY26.
On the cost side, the procurement of materials and sporting goods remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 64% of the overall expenditure. This cost increased 7.4% to Rs 2,840 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,644 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 12% to Rs 407 crore during the fiscal year.
Other expenses, including rent, franchisee fees, freight, credit card commissions and IT support charges, pushed the company's total expenditure up 4% to Rs 4,435 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,264 crore in FY25.
Despite the increase in costs, Decathlon India managed to turn profitable during the fiscal year. The company posted a net profit of Rs 63 crore in FY26, against a loss of Rs 65 crore in FY25. It also reported an EBITDA of Rs 424 crore during the year.


On a unit level, Decathlon spent Rs 0.99 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at 7.6% and 9%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 1,686 crore at the end of the fiscal year.
Decathlon has been hovering around the Rs 4,000 crore revenue mark for the past few years. To move beyond this, the company will have to expand its reach to more cities and states, something it is already working on. Its plans to expand in Europe and export more products manufactured in India could also open up new growth opportunities. The India-EU FTA may further help, depending on how the agreement shapes up. At the same time, adding more categories and bringing new products to Indian consumers will remain important. It will be interesting to see how Decathlon takes this forward and how soon it can cross the Rs 5,000 crore revenue mark.

title: Exclusive: Scripbox to convert into public company ahead of IPO plans
summary:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripbox is set to convert into a public company after passing a resolution approving the move, a step that signals its preparation for a potential public listing.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Scripbox’s board has passed a resolution to approve its conversion into a public limited company by changing its legal name from “Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited” to “Scripbox Wealth Managers Limited”.
As per the filing, the proposed initial public offering (IPO) will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) by certain existing shareholders of the company.
Founded in 2012 by Atul Shinghal and Sanjiv Singhal, Scripbox operates a digital wealth management platform that offers investment products across mutual funds, fixed deposits, US stocks, ETFs and the National Pension System (NPS), along with financial planning and advisory services.
The development comes nearly six months after Entrackr exclusively reported that Scripbox was planning to raise up to Rs 170 crore through a mix of debt and equity.
As part of the proposed fundraise, Scripbox's board had approved raising up to Rs 60 crore from a select group of investors through equity shares, preference shares and convertible instruments. It had also secured approval to raise up to Rs 110 crore through debt from banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions. 
In June this year, the company acquired the mutual fund distribution business of Delhi-NCR-based Bluechip Capital, a wealth management firm founded and led by Ravi Kohli for over 33 years. The transaction also saw Bluechip Capital's clients and employees transition to Scripbox.
Scripbox has raised over $70 million through a mix of equity and debt from investors including Accel, LetsVenture and DMI.
On the financial front, Scripbox turned profitable in FY25 with a net profit of Rs 12.7 crore, while its operating revenue grew 27% year-on-year to Rs 107.2 crore. The company is yet to disclose its FY26 financial results.

title: Specialty chemicals startup altM raises $10.3 Mn led by Rainmatter, Mela Ventures
summary:
Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM has raised $10.3 million in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures. The round also saw participation from existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact, along with VC Grid and strategic angel investors.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its manufacturing capabilities, research and development, customer qualification programmes, and engineering and commercial teams as it moves from pilot-scale production to commercial manufacturing.
Founded in 2022 by former Tesla manufacturing leaders Apoorv Garg and Yugal Raj Jain, altM is developing a specialty chemicals platform that converts agricultural residue into high-performance industrial chemicals. Bioprocessing scientist Dr Harshad Velankar later joined the company as its chief scientific officer.
The company's platform converts lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse and rice straw, into materials for beauty and personal care, textiles, industrial chemicals, construction, packaging and consumer goods.
It uses cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin to produce multiple products from a single feedstock. The process enables agricultural residue to serve as a source of industrial carbon and reduces dependence on fossil-derived raw materials.
Since raising $3.5 million in a seed round in 2023, altM has built an integrated R&D and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. The facility brings laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof.
The company has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly fivefold, commissioned its demonstration manufacturing facility and advanced six molecules to demonstration scale. Three of these have been selected for pilot plant production.
Its first products moving towards commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare applications, a cellulose-based rheology modifier and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.
altM competes with Scimplifi, Covvalent, Atomgrid and Tulon Materials, which have also raised fresh funding this year.
The latest funding will help altM scale its manufacturing operations and expand customer deployments as it seeks to build a platform for producing industrial chemicals from agricultural residue.

Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q2 FY27 results, reporting largely flat revenue during the quarter, while its losses narrowed year-on-year.
Tracxn's revenue from operations increased marginally by 0.2% to Rs 21.30 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.25 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).




Tracxn derives its operating revenue from subscription sales, which provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.38 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 22.70 crore in Q2 FY27.
Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 22.5% to Rs 23.33 crore and accounting for 85.4% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. Depreciation expenses stood at Rs 7.5 lakh, compared to Rs 4 lakh in Q2 FY26. Other expenses increased 41% to Rs 3.92 crore.

The company's total expenses rose 25% to Rs 27.32 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.86 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Despite the increase in expenses, Tracxn narrowed its net loss by 25.7% to Rs 4.13 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 5.56 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a half-yearly basis, Tracxn's revenue from operations remained largely flat at Rs 42.38 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 42.44 crore in H1 FY26. However, its net loss widened 60.8% to Rs 7.14 crore during the first half of FY27.

At the close of trading on Wednesday, Tracxn’s shares settled at Rs 32.08, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 331 crore.

title: Nykaa's profit jumps 3X to Rs 101 Cr in Q2 FY27; revenue grows 28%
summary:
Online beauty and fashion platform Nykaa reported strong growth in Q2 FY27, with its revenue from operations increasing 28% year-on-year, while its net profit surged over threefold during the quarter ended September 2026.
Nykaa's revenue from operations grew to Rs 3,006 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 2,346 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


The beauty segment continued to dominate the company's revenue, contributing Rs 2,700 crore or 90% of its operating revenue during the quarter. The fashion segment generated Rs 287 crore, accounting for 10% of the total operating revenue, while other segments contributed Rs 19 crore.

For Nykaa, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense, accounting for 56.64% of its total expenditure. This expense increased 25.7% to Rs 1,624 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,292 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. 
Employee benefit expenses grew 20% to Rs 220 crore, while depreciation expenses increased 18% to Rs 93 crore. Finance costs declined 3% to Rs 30.52 crore. Other expenses, which include marketing, technology and other overheads, increased 26% to Rs 899 crore.

The company's total expenses rose 25% to Rs 2,867 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,298 crore in Q2 FY26.
The growth in operating revenue, coupled with a slower increase in expenses, helped Nykaa improve its profitability. The company's net profit tripled to Rs 101 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 33 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.
On a half-yearly basis, Nykaa's revenue from operations increased 28.6% to Rs 5,788 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 4,501 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit also surged 214.8% to Rs 181 crore during the first half of FY27, compared to Rs 57.5 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal year.

title: Lenskart Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 36%, profit rises 2.3X to Rs 232 Cr

Eyewear brand Lenskart announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, posting a 36% year-on-year increase in consolidated operating revenue, backed by growth across both domestic and international markets. Its net profit more than doubled to Rs 232 crore during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 2,845 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,096 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from NSE.

Both domestic and international markets contributed to the company’s growth at a similar pace. Revenue from the India business grew 35.5% year-on-year to Rs 1,668 crore in Q2 FY27, while the international business recorded a 36.5% increase to Rs 1,201 crore.
On a quarterly basis, Lenskart’s revenue from operations grew 5% from Rs 2,714 crore in Q1 FY27.
On the expense side, the cost of materials remained the largest expense head, accounting for 33% of the total expenditure. It increased 31% year-on-year to Rs 854 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses also rose 25% to Rs 627 crore from Rs 503 crore in the year-ago quarter. Finance costs and depreciation were other major expense heads, taking total expenses up 22% to Rs 2,597 crore during the quarter.
The 36% growth in revenue, which outpaced the rise in total expenses, helped Lenskart more than double its net profit to Rs 232 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 103 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its EBITDA also increased 50% to Rs 622 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 21.86%.

Founded by Ritukar Vijay, Ottonomy develops AI-powered autonomous delivery robots designed to operate across indoor and outdoor environments. Its flagship product, Ottobot, uses the company’s proprietary Contextual AI technology to enable autonomous deliveries across complex facilities with minimal human intervention.
The company’s robots are designed to help hospitals and enterprises automate the transportation of medicines, medical equipment, supplies and other materials. It also works with its portfolio companies to explore international expansion opportunities, particularly in Japan. Its portfolio includes GoDesi, Pico Xpress, Uravu Labs, StackBox and Hexalog.
Ottonomy operates in the autonomous delivery and robotics segment, where companies are developing AI-powered solutions to address last-mile logistics, workforce shortages and operational efficiency across commercial and institutional settings.

title: Eggoz’s revenue grows 39% to Rs 180 Cr in FY26; losses widen to Rs 42 Cr
summary:
India’s egg market is gradually moving towards organised players, with growing consumer interest in branded products, better quality standards and traceability. This shift has opened up opportunities for companies such as Eggoz, which has built its business around sourcing eggs from farmers and supplying them through an organised distribution network.
`The company continued to expand its business in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with revenue growing 39% year-on-year. However, higher employee and advertising costs weighed on its bottom line, which pushed its losses by 83% during the fiscal year.
For context, Eggoz had reported a 78% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY25, while its net loss stood at Rs 23 crore.
Gurugram-based Eggoz’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 180 crore in FY26 from Rs 130 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC),

Founded in 2017 in Bihar by Abhishek Negi and Aditya Singh, Eggoz is operated by Nupa Technologies and follows an asset-light, farmer-led supply chain model. The company works with local poultry farmers to improve egg production, collection and distribution through technology, ensuring fresh eggs reach retailers within 24 hours. It focuses on maintaining quality and freshness while helping farmers access better technology and wider markets
Egg sales remained the company's primary revenue contributor in FY26. Eggoz also earned around Rs 6 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 186 crore during the fiscal year.
A look at the expense structure shows that procurement of raw materials remained the largest cost component, which rose 38% to Rs 142 crore in FY26 from Rs 102.7 crore in the previous fiscal. It accounted for over 62% of the company's total expenditure.
Employee benefit expenses increased 50% to Rs 30.8 crore during FY26 from Rs 20.5 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses saw a sharper jump of 2.9X to Rs 30 crore from Rs 10.5 crore in the previous fiscal.
Transportation costs also rose 32.2% to Rs 7.8 crore, while other expenses such as legal & professional, travelling, collectively added around Rs 17 crore to the total cost.
Consequently, Eggoz's total expenditure increased 48.% year-on-year to Rs 228 crore in FY26 from Rs 154 crore in FY25.
Despite strong revenue growth, a sharper increase in employee benefit and advertising expenses pushed Eggoz's net loss up 83% to Rs 42 crore in FY26 from Rs 23 crore in the previous fiscal.

Eggoz reported a ROCE of -40.6% and an EBITDA margin of -24.44%, with an EBITDA loss of Rs 44 crore in FY26. At the unit level, the company spent Rs 1.27 for every rupee of operating revenue. As of March 2026, it had cash and bank balances of Rs 33 crore and total current assets of Rs 45 crore.
Eggoz has raised over $32 million across multiple funding rounds to date. The company raised $20 million in a round led by Gaja Capital in June 2025, following an $8.8 million Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures in December 2022.

title: Fintech infra startup OneStack raises Rs 12.5 Cr from Shepherd's Hill, others
summary:
Fintech infrastructure startup OneStack has raised Rs 12.5 crore from new investor Shepherd's Hill and existing backers Pentathlon Ventures and AVNM Ventures.
The Mumbai-based startup had previously raised  $2 million in a Series A round in March 2025, led by Pentathlon Ventures, with participation from Yatra Angel Network and existing investors 100Unicorns and Venture Catalysts. With this round, OneStack has raised Rs 45 crore across four funding rounds.
The proceeds will be used to expand its presence among cooperative banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), alongside product development in payments, core banking and regulatory compliance, the company said in a press release.
Founded by Amit Kapoor in 2019, OneStack provides technology infrastructure that enables smaller financial institutions to offer digital banking services without building their own systems. Its platform includes mobile banking, UPI issuing and merchant acquiring, QR payments, debit card management and its OneCBS core banking system.
The company said cooperative banks using its platform can now operate as UPI issuers and acquirers directly with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), under their own bank handles. This enables them to issue UPI IDs to customers, onboard merchants and settle payments through their own payment rails, while retaining customer relationships, transaction data and merchant discount rate (MDR) revenue.
OneStack plans to extend its platform to NBFCs with tools for customer verification and fraud reporting. Its compliance suite includes integration with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The company is also an Aadhaar OVSE technology service provider, has integrated eKYC Setu and holds RuPay debit card issuance certification and SU3J licenses under credit bureaus.
OneStack has also partnered with a large private sector bank that sponsors more than 250 cooperative banks. The partnership will provide a route to offer UPI issuing, merchant acquiring and its wider banking platform across the network.
The company claims to serve more than 200 banks across India, including state cooperative banks, district central cooperative banks (DCCBs) and non-scheduled urban cooperative banks (NSUCBs).
India's cooperative banking network presents a sizable market for technology providers. NABARD's 2024-25 annual report records 34 state cooperative banks and 351 DCCBs, which together operated nearly 15,900 branches as of March 2025.
Several startups are offering technology infrastructure to cooperative banks and other financial institutions to support their digital transformation. These include core banking software, mobile banking applications, payment systems and compliance tools.
Another player, RUGR Fintech, raised $5 million in pre-Series A funding in September 2025, led by Vikasa India EIF I Fund, to expand its digital payments and rural banking infrastructure. Freshworks reported a 14% year-on-year growth in revenue to $245.4 million in Q3 CY26, compared to $215.1 million in the corresponding quarter last year. The Nasdaq-listed SaaS company also turned profitable, posting a net profit of $18.3 million against a net loss of $4.7 million in Q3 CY25.
The company’s gross profit increased 15% to $209.4 million during the quarter from $182.2 million in the year-ago period. Its gross margin improved to 85.3% from 84.7%.
On the operational front, Freshworks reported an operating profit of $28.2 million, compared to an operating loss of $7.5 million in Q3 CY25. Its operating margin stood at 11.5% against a negative margin of 3.5% in the corresponding quarter last year.
The company’s non-GAAP operating income rose 62% to $73.2 million, while its non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 29.8% from 21%.
On the expenditure front, sales and marketing expenses declined 2.5% to $98.5 million. Research and development expenses increased 7.8% to $44.7 million, while general and administrative expenses fell 19% to $38.2 million. Consequently, total operating expenses declined 4.4% to $181.2 million from $189.6 million in Q3 CY25.
Freshworks generated $77.7 million in cash from operating activities during the quarter, compared to $63.5 million in the year-ago period. Adjusted free cash flow rose 29% to $73.9 million, with its margin improving to 30.1% from 26.6%.
The company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities worth $697.3 million as of September 30, 2026.
Freshworks also crossed $1 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) after the close of the third quarter, ahead of its earlier year-end estimate. Customers contributing more than $100,000 in ARR increased 25% year-on-year to 1,821, while its net dollar retention rate stood at 104%.
For Q4 CY26, Freshworks expects revenue between $253.5-$254.5 million. For the full calendar year 2026, it has projected revenue of $965 million to $966 million, representing approximately 15% annual growth.

title: EloElo Group raises $80 Mn in Series C led by Hornbill Capital, NBCUniversal
summary:
Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group has raised $80 million in a Series C funding round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. The round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing investors Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners and others.
The fresh capital will be used to fund original content across languages, support the international launch of its micro drama platform Story TV, and expand investments in Dolphin AI, its agentic AI creative suite.
Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey, EloElo Group operates Story TV, a micro drama platform, alongside Master, a micro learning platform, Dolphin AI and Voxy AI, an AI companion agent. Story TV offers over 5,000 micro dramas across six languages, with a new drama launched every three hours. The platform records 95 minutes of daily time spent per user, according to the company.
The company owns the content, distribution and AI-powered production engine behind its entertainment business. Across its apps, EloElo Group has over 40 million monthly active users and has crossed 300 million installs.
The latest funding round takes the company's total capital raised to $130 million which includes a $13.5 million Series B round raised in April 2025.
EloElo said it achieved multi-fold revenue growth over the past year and has scaled with profitable unit economics. EloElo began monetising in May 2024 and reported revenue of Rs 69.5 crore in FY25, with losses remaining largely flat. Its FY26 results are yet to be filed.
Micro dramas are among the fastest-growing formats in global entertainment. According to Omdia, the industry is expected to generate $14 billion globally by the end of 2026. In India, Redseer estimates that 40 million people paid for a micro drama at least once in FY26, while Lumikai's State of India Interactive Media Report projects the market to reach $4.5 billion by 2030.
EloElo Group said it will also use the fresh capital to expand its content slate, with a focus on premium originals, and take its micro drama business to international markets, including the US.
EloElo Group’s Master competes with Seekho, which is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed and raised $28 million in a Series B round last September. title: Bakingo's revenue crosses Rs 400 Cr in FY26, losses double
summary:
India's online bakery market has grown beyond traditional birthday cakes, with customised desserts, premium baked goods and quick delivery becoming an increasingly important part of the celebration and gifting economy. Bakingo has tapped into this demand to build a business generating over Rs 400 crore revenue in FY26. However, higher operating costs continued to weigh on its bottom line, with the company's losses doubling to Rs 37 crore during the last fiscal year.
Bakingo’s revenue from operations grew by 35% year-on-year to Rs 405.8 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 300.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies.

Founded in 2016 by Himanshu Chawla, Shrey Sehgal and Suman Patra, Bakingo operates an online bakery business offering a range of cakes and desserts, including cheesecakes, gourmet cakes and jar cakes. The company has a presence across 30-plus cities, supported by a network of over 100 kitchens and a catalogue of more than 100 products. Sales of these bakery products remained its sole source of revenue for the firm in FY26.
It also earned Rs 7.3 crore from interests on investments and fixed deposits, which pushed its overall income to Rs 413.65 crore in FY26.
For the bakery firm, raw material procurement for cakes and desserts remained its largest expense, accounting for over 43% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 40% year-on-year to Rs 194.45 crore in FY26 from Rs 138.7 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Employee benefit expenses also rose 40% to Rs 31.6 crore, while advertising expenses increased 35% to Rs 75.4 crore. Commission and platform fees surged over 39% to Rs 53 crore. Other overheads, including delivery and transportation, outsourced support, and power and fuel costs, further added to the expenditure.
Overall, Bakingo's total expenses increased 38.7% to Rs 450.5 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 324.7 crore in FY25.
Despite recording 35% revenue growth in FY26, Bakingo's bottom line remained under pressure as operating expenses grew at a faster pace, resulting in its losses more than doubling to Rs 36.9 crore in the fiscal year.

Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -39% and -7.48%, respectively. On a unit level, Bakingo spent Rs 1.11 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its total current assets stood at Rs 86 crore, including cash and bank balance of Rs 30 crore during the last fiscal year.
Bakingo has raised $26.5 million to date across two funding rounds. This includes a Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) funding round in August this year, led by existing investor Faering Capital at a valuation of $173 million, as exclusively reported by Entrackr.
When Theobroma was acquired for a valuation of close to Rs 2600 crore in FY 24-25, it was also clocking revenues in the same range as Bakingo in FY26. Perhaps it is those numbers that have driven the firm to invest strongly in advertising and growth, but the valuation gap is significant. The starkest of course is the brand itself, which occupies a distinctly massier segment than Theobroma. That will also make it tougher to deliver margins that can meet investor expectations. We really think there is a long haul ahead for Bakingo in a part of the market that has little by way of protection, and the firm needs to think long and hard about its next steps.

title: Razorpay receives SEBI approval for IPO
summary:
Fintech unicorn Razorpay has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to sources familiar with the development.
The Bengaluru-based company had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI in June 2026.
According to an Economic Times report, Razorpay is targeting to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore through its IPO at an expected valuation of $5 billion (Rs 49,000-50,000 crore).
As per sources, the company expected to file its final IPO papers before March 2027.
Media reports indicate that Razorpay has roped in Axis Capital, Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan and Citi as bankers for its proposed IPO.
Razorpay was last valued at $7.5 billion in 2021, when it raised $375 million during the peak of the funding cycle. Since then, the company has undertaken several strategic initiatives ahead of its public market debut.
In April 2025, Razorpay converted into a public limited company as part of its IPO preparations. Later that year, it completed its reverse flip to India, a process that involved shifting its domicile from the US to India. The company paid around $150 million in taxes related to the transition.
Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay provides payment gateway services to businesses. Over the years, it has expanded into business banking, lending and payment solutions for merchants.
Most recently, Razorpay received the final Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate in GIFT City, Gujarat. The licence will allow the fintech company to offer payment services to businesses operating in the International Financial Services Centre.
Entrackr has reached out to Razorpay for comments. The story will be updated once the company responds.

summary:
Managed workspace solutions provider IndiQube announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 35% year-on-year increase in operating revenue. The Bengaluru-based company’s net loss narrowed 80% to Rs 5.90 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.
IndiQube’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 350 crore in Q2 FY26, according to financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

In the first half of FY27, IndiQube’s revenue from operations grew 35.7% to Rs 895 crore from Rs 659.5 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.
Founded in 2015, IndiQube offers managed workspace solutions to startups, enterprises and SMEs across major Indian cities. The company also recorded Rs 20 crore in other income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 492 crore compared to Rs 367 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the managed office provider, depreciation on leases remained its largest cost component, increasing 25% year-on-year to Rs 195 crore in Q2 FY27. Finance costs stood at Rs 129 crore, while employee benefit expenses declined marginally to Rs 24.5 crore.
Meanwhile, the cost of materials increased 11.5% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 26 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Overall, IndiQube’s total expenses increased 23.5% year-on-year to Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 405 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the bottom line, the company narrowed its net loss by 80.3% to Rs 5.90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 29.90 crore in the year-ago quarter.
On a sequential basis, revenue from operations grew 11.6% to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 423 crore in Q1 FY27. Meanwhile, the company’s net loss narrowed 74.8% to Rs 5.90 crore from Rs 23.40 crore during the same period.

title: Snitch revenue grows 68% to Rs 835 Cr in FY26; posts Rs 27 Cr loss
summary:
India’s men’s fast-fashion market has shifted significantly over the past few years, with consumers becoming more experimental in their style choices and fashion preferences. Snitch is among the brands that have capitalised on this trend, growing its revenue 3.4X over the past two fiscal years while keeping its losses relatively contained.
Snitch’s revenue from operations grew 67.7% year-on-year to Rs 835 crore in FY26 from Rs 498 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded in 2020 by Siddharth Dungarwal, Snitch sells trendy men’s apparel and accessories through its website and app. Apparel and accessories remain the company’s sole revenue stream. It also earned Rs 14 crore in other income, largely through interest on deposits and long-term investments, taking its total income to Rs 849 crore in FY26.

The company has also entered the quick commerce segment as it looks to expand its reach and delivery capabilities. At the same time, Snitch has been expanding its offline presence. According to its website, the brand operates 142 stores across India, including in metro and Tier II cities.
For the D2C fashion brand, procurement of apparel and accessories remained the largest cost component, accounting for around 51% of its overall expenditure. In line with the growth in scale, this expense increased 92.2% to Rs 444 crore in FY26 from Rs 231 crore in FY25.
Snitch spent Rs 108 crore on advertising and marketing during the year, while employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 81 crore. Marketplace charges, rent, delivery and other overheads also added to the cost base. As a result, its total expenditure increased 71.9% to Rs 873 crore in FY26 from Rs 508 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing slightly faster than revenue, Snitch reported a net loss of Rs 27 crore in FY26. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.05 to earn a rupee in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -8.6% and -3%, respectively.

Snitch has raised over $53 million to date, including a $40 million Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset in June 2025.
For a company that has scaled its revenue to Rs 835 crore in just a few years, keeping losses at Rs 27 crore is a relatively encouraging sign. While the business is yet to turn profitable, its growing scale, expanding offline presence and entry into quick commerce provide room for further growth. The bigger question now is whether Snitch can convert this scale into sustainable profits without letting its costs grow faster than revenue.
Snitch operates in an increasingly competitive D2C fashion market, competing with brands such as The Souled Store, Rare Rabbit and Wrogn. The Souled Store reported a 37% growth in revenue to Rs 492 crore in FY25, while premium fashion brand Rare Rabbit reported revenue of Rs 818 crore. Meanwhile, Wrogn, backed by Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, reported revenue of Rs 244 crore in FY26.

summary:
Deeptech robotics startup Armatrix has raised Rs 67.28 crore in a seed funding round led by UK-based Crane Venture Partners, along with participation from new and existing investors.
The fresh funding comes less than a year after its pre-seed round and values the company nearly 5X higher than its previous round.
In January 2026, Armatrix had raised $2.1 million in a pre-seed round led by pi Ventures, with participation from Inuka Capital, Boundless Ventures, Boost VC, Turbostart and gradCapital.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company has allotted 4,070 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,64,900 per share, along with 10 equity shares, to raise the capital.
The funding round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi-based company likely to raise more capital in subsequent tranches.
Crane Venture Partners led the round with an investment of Rs 40 crore. Existing investor pi Ventures infused Rs 15 crore, followed by gradCapital with Rs 4.52 crore, Boundless Ventures with Rs 2.5 crore and Inuka Capital with Rs 2.37 crore. NKSquared also joined the round with an investment of Rs 2.37 crore, marking its entry into the company.
Among other investors, AL Trust, Saurabh Chandra, Unacademy co-founder Roman Saini and existing investor Narayan Rangarajan collectively invested Rs 67 lakh in the round.
According to Entrackr's estimates, Armatrix's valuation jumped 4.8X to Rs 360 crore in the seed round from Rs 75 crore in its pre-seed round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds for business expansion and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2024 by Vishrant Dave, Prateesh Awasthi and Ayush Ranjan, Bengaluru-based Armatrix develops snake-like robotic manipulators for operations in hazardous and confined industrial spaces. Its technology is designed for inspection and maintenance across sectors such as shipbuilding, nuclear energy, oil and gas, and aviation, reducing the need for human workers to enter dangerous spaces.
According to Moneycontrol, Armatrix was in talks to raise $15 million in a seed round led by Crane Venture Partners.
The company remained at the pre-revenue stage in FY26 and reported a net loss of Rs 3.05 crore.

V3 Ventures has also invested in consumer and food businesses, including Go Zero, Crème Castle, Dil Foods, Super You and Salad Days.

summary:

Bengaluru-based edtech unicorn’s revenue from operations grew 17.6% to Rs 267 crore in FY26 from Rs 227 crore in the previous fiscal, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
Tuition fees remained its largest revenue source for Vedantu, growing 16.8% to Rs 222 crore from Rs 190 crore in FY25. Revenue from books, uniforms and other products increased 31.8% to Rs 29 crore, while e-learning project income stood at Rs 6.3 crore during the last fiscal year.
With non-operating income of Rs 3.8 crore, the firm posted a total income of Rs 270 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026.

On the expense side, employee benefit expenses, the largest cost component, declined 12.8% to Rs 191 crore in FY26 from Rs 219.5 crore in FY25. It also includes Rs 7.2 crore as ESOP cost (non-cash. Contract and outsourced resources costs surged 54.3% to Rs 71 crore, while depreciation expenses declined 5.8% to Rs 65 crore.
Advertising and promotional expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 29 crore, whereas technology expenses stood at Rs 12 crore . Overall, Vedantu’s total expenses remained largely flat at Rs 442 crore in FY26.
With the decent growth coupled with stable expenses, Vedantu’s losses before exceptional items and tax decreased by 18.6% to Rs 171 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 210 crore in FY25.  
Note: We have excluded exceptional income and expenses arising from changes in the fair valuation of consideration payable (liability towards future obligations) in both FY25 and FY26 to present a clearer picture of the company's financial performance.
At the unit level, the company also improved its expense-to-operating revenue ratio. As of March 2026, the company had cash and bank balances of Rs 77.25 crore, while its total current assets stood at Rs 160 crore.
The improvement in pre-exceptional performance comes as Vedantu continues to compete in a more consolidated edtech market. Byju’s has collapsed, while Unacademy has scaled back its operations, leaving Physics Wallah as a key competitor in the online education and test-preparation space. Unlike the earlier funding-led expansion phase, the next phase of competition is likely to depend more on student outcomes, pricing and the ability to build a sustainable business.
Vedantu raised $11 million from internal investors in September 2025 as part of a larger round led by ABC World Asia, with participation from Accel India and Omidyar. The funding could support its efforts to strengthen its offerings and compete with Physics Wallah.
The improvement in Vedantu’s core performance suggests that the company may be entering a more stable phase after the difficult period faced by the edtech sector. Its ability to grow revenue while keeping overall expenses largely flat offers a positive sign. The focus now will be on sustaining this growth, improving cash flows and building a stronger business as competition grows.
The fact that PW is now a public firm probably is not the disadvantage it could be for Vedantu, as it can still chase opportunities without the glare of market appraisal hanging over it. Though some would say being public has made PW more disciplined. We believe Vedantu definitely has it in it to spring a surprise yet, which could come as early as the end of the ongoing financial year (FY27) or next year (FY28).

title: DeHaat posts Rs 2,715 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
Several agritech companies that initially started as marketplaces for selling agricultural inputs and outputs are now moving towards building their own brands. The shift is aimed at improving margins, gaining better control over pricing, and reducing dependence on third-party products.
Full-stack agritech platform DeHaat has pursued this strategy over the past few years by expanding its portfolio of in-house brands. The shift towards building its own brands appears to have involved a near-term trade-off on growth, with operating revenue declining nearly 10% in FY26, even as the company continued to reshape its business. The firm’s net loss also widened in FY26 as it continued to invest in its in-house brands
DeHaat's revenue from operations fell 9.8% to Rs 2,715 crore in FY26 from Rs 3,010 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The sale of agricultural inputs, including seeds, fertilisers and other farm-related products, contributed Rs 517 crore, accounting for around 19% of its operating revenue. The remaining revenue came from its agricultural output business, which includes staples, chillies and consumer-facing initiatives such as Farm Plus and HonestFarms.
India continued to be DeHaat's largest market, contributing 83% of its total revenue. The remaining income came from international markets, including the UK, Europe, the Middle East, Thailand and Russia.

On the cost side, procurement of materials remained the firm's largest expense, accounting for nearly 80% of its overall expenditure. As business scale moderated, this cost also declined by 11.7% to Rs 2,390 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses fell 9.1% to Rs 159 crore in the same period.
Other expenses, including transportation, rent, warehousing, sales and branding, along with legal and administrative overheads, took the company's total expenditure to Rs 2,972 crore in FY26, against Rs 3,242 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Despite an 8.3% decline in overall expenses, the revenue fall put further pressure on the company's bottom line, resulting in DeHaat's losses increasing by 11.4% to Rs 224 crore in FY26 from Rs 201 crore in FY25.
Note: We have excluded the Rs 578 crore income recorded from the change in the fair value of preference shares to present a clearer picture of the company's financial performance.
At a unit level, DeHaat spent Rs 1.09 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -53.9%, while its EBITDA margin was recorded at 6%. The company also had current assets of around Rs 1,000 crore at the end of the fiscal year.
The agritech sector has been navigating a more measured growth phase since the funding boom of 2021-22, with startups placing greater emphasis on sustainable business models. DeHaat’s move beyond its original marketplace model and focus on building in-house brands could help it improve margins, strengthen customer relationships and gain greater control over its business. While the transition has affected near-term growth and profitability, it could open up new opportunities over time. The key question is how quickly DeHaat can scale these brands and translate them into a stronger growth and profitability engine.

Lending disbursals also grew 34% to Rs 1,082.6 crore from Rs 807.1 crore during the same period.
For the fintech firm, payment gateway charges remained MobiKwik's largest expense in Q2 FY27, accounting for over 42% of its total costs. Employee benefit expenses surged 59% to Rs 56.2 crore during the quarter.
The company also reported financial guarantee costs of Rs 28.3 crore, while legal, advertising and marketing, finance and other overheads contributed to its overall expenditure. MobiKwik's total expenses stood at Rs 290.9 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally lower than Rs 296 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Mobikwik reported its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 11.8 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 28.6 crore in the same quarter last year. On a sequential basis, its profit increased 55% from Rs 7.6 crore in Q1 FY27.
The Gurugram-based firm also reported its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of Rs 22.7 crore, compared to an EBITDA loss of Rs 6.4 crore in Q2 FY26. This marked the company's fourth consecutive profitable quarter.

title: Indian startup funding nosedives 47.5% to $678 Mn in October
summary:
Indian startups raised $678 million in October, a 47.5% month-on-month decline, as the absence of large funding rounds dragged overall investments. No startup secured a funding round of $100 million or more, while only Tessolve and Even Healthcare crossed the $50 million mark. Growth stage deals received a boost from rounds raised by Boldfit, DailyObjects, RapidCanvas and Nat Habit, while early stage funding saw moderate participation from Auxo AI, Cent, Mesa and Matiks.

The month saw no reported layoffs, while Jio Platforms made a high-profile stock market debut, followed by listings of Zetwerk and AceVector, the operator of Snapdeal. Merger and acquisition activity, however, remained limited to select sectors.
[Overview]
According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $678 million in funding during October. This amount included 20 growth and late-stage deals totalling $414.6 million, along with 79 early-stage deals worth $263 million. Additionally, there were 9 undisclosed deals during the period.
Y-o-Y and M-o-M trend
October 2026 saw a sharp decline in startup funding compared to the same month last year. Total funding fell 60.8% to $677.8 million from $1.73 billion in October 2025. On a month-on-month basis, funding declined 47.5% from $1.29 billion in September. February was the strongest month for funding in 2026, with startups raising around $2 billion, followed by June, which also recorded around $2 billion. October’s decline came amid a lack of larger deals, with no startup raising $100 million or more during the month.

[Top 10 growth-stage deals]
Growth and late-stage startups saw activity across sectors in October, led by semiconductor solutions provider Tessolve Semiconductor, which raised $75 million, followed by healthtech startup Even Healthcare with $50 million. Sports and fitness brand Boldfit secured $42 million, while lifestyle brand DailyObjects and enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas raised $35 million and $29 million, respectively. Advanced materials manufacturer Simplify raised $25 million, followed by robotics startup Origin with $20 million. Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit and AI startups Simplismart and Live2.ai raised $15 million, $14 million and $14 million, respectively.

[Top 10 early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups saw funding across AI, healthtech, edtech and gaming in October, led by enterprise AI startup AuxoAI, which raised $20.7 million, followed by healthtech startup Cent with $15 million. Mesa School of Business and Confido Health secured $12.5 million each, while gaming startup Spill Games raised $10.5 million. AI video platform Clueso, quantum computing startup Quanfluence and social gaming platform Matiks received $10 million each. Nutrition brand Ace Blend raised $9.91 million, while edtech startup byteXL secured $9 million to expand its technology training programmes.

[Mergers and acquisitions]
Indian startups recorded five acquisitions in October across SaaS, healthtech, cybersecurity and FMCG. Freshworks acquired AI startup Robusta, while healthtech startup Cent acquired Medsee and cybersecurity firm Protectt.ai acquired AIShield. In the FMCG sector, Marico acquired Satya Nutraceuticals for $110 million. Meanwhile, Hoola Health acquired UpTodd, marking continued consolidation in the healthtech sector.

[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding in October with $420 million across 52 deals, accounting for 61.97% of the total capital raised. Delhi-NCR followed with $110.26 million across 18 deals, while Mumbai startups raised $57.53 million across 11 deals. Hyderabad secured $41.22 million across five deals, followed by Bhubaneswar with $11.5 million from a single deal.
E-commerce startups led sector-wise funding with $182.69 million across 27 deals, followed by AI startups with $131.12 million across 22 deals. Healthtech companies raised $104.61 million across 13 deals, while semiconductor startups secured $75 million in a single deal. Manufacturers raised $36.67 million across four deals, rounding out the top five segments.
[Series-wise deals]
Series B startups led funding in October with $209.34 million across 10 deals, followed by Series A companies with $135.35 million across 17 deals. Seed-stage startups raised $80.41 million across 41 deals, while Series C companies secured $61.5 million across three deals. Pre-Series A startups raised $23.24 million across seven deals.

[Key hirings and departures]
October saw key leadership appointments across startups and investment firms, with Mayank Khanduja joining Bessemer Venture Partners as a partner and Manas Poddar taking charge as CBO at OTPless. Sanjeev Bikhchandani continued as MD and group CEO at Info Edge, while Kiran U joined Bellatrix Aerospace as CFO. Other notable appointments included Basant Dhawan as CMO at Shoonya by Finvasia, Medhavi Singh as India country head at Aleph and Kamaldeep Singh as CEO at Infost Energy. Meanwhile, Sanjeev Bikhchandani and Mithun Sacheti were among the key departures, from Info Edge and Nazara Technologies, respectively.
[Tends]
Zorit comeback: Zorit (formerly Bijnis) raised funding from investors including Sparoww Capital and Info Edge Capital, which had written off its entire investment in the startup in 2023.
Vama funding: Spiritual tech startup Vama raised funding from the Dainik Bhaskar family office, which could be among its first recorded startup investments.
Quick home services race: Snabbit recorded an NTV of Rs 72 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally ahead of Urban Company's InstaHelp at Rs 71 crore. Snabbit reported a burn of Rs 142 crore against InstaHelp's adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore, although the figures may not be directly comparable.
Burma Burma follows Subway India with IPO filing: Hunger Pangs, the operator of Burma Burma, filed its DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of up to Rs 600 crore, with no OFS. The filing follows that of Subway India operator EverBrands India in September.

[Conclusion]
October’s funding slowdown reflects a more selective investment environment, with investors prioritising stronger business fundamentals and clearer paths to profitability. Indian startups have raised nearly $11 billion so far in 2026. If funding averages $1 billion in each of the remaining two months, the annual total could cross the $13 billion recorded in 2023. title: iD Fresh Food nears Rs 900 Cr revenue in FY26; profit before exceptional items surges 3X
summary:
Ready-to-cook food is becoming a staple in Indian kitchens as consumers seek convenience without giving up home-cooked meals. iD Fresh Food has built its business around this growing preference, clocking nearly Rs 900 crore in revenue in FY26 while remaining profitable.
iD Fresh Food’s revenue from operations increased 27.7% year-on-year to Rs 870 crore in FY26 from Rs 681 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The Bengaluru-based company manufactures ready-to-cook products such as idli and dosa batter and parathas. It also trades in food products, including curd, paneer, coffee, specialty batter and other food items.
iD Fresh operates manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Haryana and Ajman in the UAE. Manufactured products such as parathas and various batters contributed Rs 671 crore, accounting for 75% of its total operating income. The remaining income came from traded goods, including dairy products, chapatis, beverages, and frozen fruits.

The firm also earned Rs 8 crore in other income, primarily from interest on current investments, taking its total income to Rs 879 crore in FY26.
Raw material procurement remained the largest cost component, accounting for 49% of the company's total expenditure. This expense increased 18.3% to Rs 394 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also rose 16% to Rs 168 crore.
The company spent Rs 70 crore on advertising in FY25. Other expenses, including legal, rent, freight, transportation and overheads, pushed its total expenditure up 20.5% to Rs 801 crore in FY26 from Rs 665 crore in FY25.
Despite the rise in costs, strong revenue growth helped iD Fresh improve its profit before tax and exceptional items to Rs 79 crore in FY26 from Rs 24 crore in FY25.
Note: The analysis excludes exceptional items worth Rs 713 crore, primarily related to changes in the fair valuation of preference shares and gains arising from the deconsolidation of a subsidiary. These accounting adjustments are excluded to provide a clearer picture of the company's business performance.
iD Fresh Food reported EBITDA of Rs 111 crore in FY26, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at 17.4% and 13%, respectively. Its total current assets stood at Rs 250 crore during the fiscal year.

iD Fresh Food has established itself as one of the early players in India's ready-to-cook food market, building a sizeable business around products that were once largely prepared at home. However, the opportunity also comes with challenges. The success of the category has attracted several competitors, putting pressure on pricing, margins and distribution. For iD Fresh, the next phase of growth will depend not just on expanding its product portfolio and reach but also on making its distribution more efficient and building stronger consumer loyalty.
The challenge for iD Fresh is no longer proving that Indians are willing to pay for convenience, but convincing them to choose its products over an expanding list of alternatives.
